programmes.d: Some of the biggest breakthroughs as we approach 2050, are happening in medicine.
Even before 2050, man and machine are meeting in ways only dreamed of by sci-fi writers.
In 2050 we’ll be living underwater, and plans are underway to live in caves on the Moon’s surface.

programmes.t: Voyage of the Continents: Asia: Rising Mountains and Sinking Countries
programmes.d: Effects from the Indo-Asian collision were felt thousands of kilometers away. The deforming pressure towards the East created Indochina, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan. How else could the remains of primitive Asians have been found in Java?

programmes.t: Voyage of the Continents: Europe: Tropical Beginnings
programmes.d: One billion years ago there was just one great continent on earth. It began to break apart and Europe drifted away. Tectonic collisions, tropical vegetation, inland seas and hot lagoons are what temperate contemporary Europe is made of.

programmes.t: Voyage of the Continents: Europe: A Turbulent Future
programmes.d: Over time, the Atlantic Ocean widened. Then Africa moved north, struck Europe and birthed the Alps. Erosion, volcanic activity, and ice ages fashioned an extraordinarily rich and varied continent, ready for the arrival of human beings.

programmes.t: Voyage of the Continents: The Origins of Africa
programmes.d: Africa is Mother Earth. Gondwana, the first, single, landmass broke apart into today's continents, but its heart is Africa. Land of rifts, lakes and volcanoes, Africa's mineral deposits testify to its eons-old history.
Humans refine and evolve weapons designs over the millennia to gain the upper hand.
Pioneering breakthroughs from across the globe shape the ability to travel.
The first data-recording device from over 5,000 years ago; how weaving creates binary code.
From living in caves to grand mansions, shelter has always been high on the list of priorities.

The Rockies. Magnificent and awe-inspiring mysterious, the Rockies are one of the longest mountain ranges in the world. Naked Science investigates the geological processes that build these massive mountains.
Throughout history, the earth has been bombarded from space. Asteroid impacts have caused mass extinctions – including the dinosaur wipe out.
Naked Science investigates the violent cosmological forces that create planets and discover what it is that makes a planet a planet.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Stars Above
programmes.d: The life cycle of stars reveal to us the past and the future of Earth and ourselves.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Dark Side
programmes.d: In terms of the Universe, we know we don't know much, especially when it comes to dark matter and dark energy. Scientists are devoting so much of their time to discovering as much as the possibly can about this mysterious matter.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Living with Space
programmes.d: Astronauts and Cosmonauts train and study for years to work and live aboard the International Space Station. With this wealth of experience and insight behind them what do they think when they return to Earth?

Our atmosphere is an unbelievably complex machine that protects us from the vacuum of space, shelters us from harmful radiation and allows us and the biosphere to breath; we need to learn much more about it so we can better it.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Flight Status
programmes.d: The next 12 months will see an intense rise in flight tests, demonstration launches and high priority flights. Some are on time others are not. We check the flight status of some of this new hardware and these new capabilities.
